**G20 countries that satisfy all four criteria**

| Country | Population growth (2008‑2009) | Birth rate (2008‑2009) | Life expectancy (2008‑2009) | 2009 unemployment rate | Meets all criteria? |
|---------|------------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------|------------------------|---------------------|
| **Canada** | **+0.170 %** | **10.28 /1 000** | **81.23 yrs** | **6.16 %** | **✓** |
| **France** | **+0.549 %** | **12.57 /1 000** | **80.98 yrs** | **9.39 %** | **✓** |
| **Australia** | **+1.195 %** | **12.47 /1 000** | **81.63 yrs** | **5.60 %** | **✓** |

*All other G20 members either have a negative population‑growth rate, a birth‑rate below 10/1 000, a life expectancy below 80 yrs, or a 2009 unemployment rate of 9.5 % or higher.*

---

### Sources

**Demographic data (University of Toronto – G8 & G20 Demographics fact sheet, 2010)**  

- Canada: population, growth, birth‑rate, life expectancy – *“Canada 33,930,800 0.170 % 10.28/1 000 81.23 years”*【6†L14-L17】  
- France: *“France 64,057,792 0.549 % 12.57/1 000 80.98 years”*【6†L15-L18】  
- Australia: *“Australia 21,262,641 1.195 % 12.47/1 000 81.63 years”*【6†L18-L21】

**Unemployment data (University of Toronto – G8 & G20 Economic Indicators fact sheet, 2010)**  

- Canada: 2009 unemployment – *“Canada … 6.16 %”*【7†L11-L12】  
- France: 2009 unemployment – *“France … 9.39 %”*【7†L12-L13】  
- Australia: 2009 unemployment – *“Australia … 5.60 %”*【7†L13-L14】

---

### How the countries fare against each criterion

| Criterion | Canada | France | Australia |
|-----------|--------|--------|-----------|
| Population growth > 0 % | +0.170 % ✔ | +0.549 % ✔ | +1.195 % ✔ |
| Birth rate > 10/1 000 | 10.28 ✔ | 12.57 ✔ | 12.47 ✔ |
| Life expectancy > 80 yrs | 81.23 ✔ | 80.98 ✔ | 81.63 ✔ |
| 2009 unemployment < 9.5 % | 6.16 ✔ | 9.39 ✔ | 5.60 ✔ |

Thus, **Canada, France, and Australia** are the only G20 members that meet *all* of the specified conditions.
